Newark by the numbers

Which Newark office sends the property tax bill?

The City of Newark Department of Finance bills and collects it, and Essex County is the county that hears assessment appeals. Inside Finance, the Assessments unit decides what real estate is taxable, keeps a tax map for every parcel and records ownership and mortgage changes. Revenue Collections sends the bills, takes the payments and runs enforcement when taxes go unpaid.

To learn what a Newark property owes, call customer service Monday through Friday, 9 am to 4 pm, except holidays. The tax lines are 973-733-3791, 973-733-3792, 973-733-3962, 973-733-8098 and 973-733-3978. The city's Payment Center also takes online tax payments by credit card, debit card or electronic check.

When are Newark property taxes due?

Installments are due on February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, the quarterly dates that apply across New Jersey. Late amounts can carry interest of up to 8 percent on the first $1,500 and up to 18 percent above that, plus a penalty of up to 6 percent for delinquencies above $10,000 when the fiscal year closes.

Newark applies a partial payment to the oldest quarter outstanding. A homeowner who owes the first three quarters and sends money in September sees it go against the first quarter's principal and interest, so the later quarters stay open. That matters for a seller, because the payoff on the closing statement can be larger than a quick tally of the latest bill suggests.

What happens to a Newark house when taxes go unpaid?

The city sells a tax lien certificate on it. Newark runs a standard tax sale for prior years' taxes and charges that are still owing, and an accelerated tax sale for the current year's charges that remain due after the statutory date of November 10. Its Finance page cites N.J.S.A. 54:5-19 for taxes outstanding from the prior year.

  • The buyer of the certificate holds a lien and does not take title at the auction.
  • A town holder can sue to foreclose six months after the sale, and a private holder can sue after two years.
  • An owner can demand in writing, before final judgment, that the property go to a sheriff's sale so any equity is protected.
  • Redemption stays open until the Superior Court enters a judgment barring it.

Our New Jersey tax sale guide covers redemption costs and the equity demand in detail.

Where do I file an appeal of a Newark assessment?

File with the Essex County Board of Taxation on Form A-1, together with the comparable sales form that goes with it. The petition must be filed and received by April 1, or by May 1 when a municipal revaluation or reassessment has been done. For a property assessed above $1,000,000, the owner may file directly with the State Tax Court instead.

The burden sits with the owner. You have to show that the assessed value is unreasonable compared with a market value standard. An assessment counts as excessive or discriminatory only if it fails both the true market value standard and the common level range, which is plus or minus 15 percent of the district's average ratio.

  • A judgment from the county board can be appealed to the Tax Court of New Jersey within 45 days.
  • An added or omitted assessment, which arises when changes are made to a property after October 1, is appealed on Form AA-1.
  • An added assessment above $750,000 in total may go directly to the Tax Court.

What does Newark look like for a house seller?

Puritans from the New Haven Colony settled Newark in 1666, and it became a city on April 11, 1836. It is the county seat of Essex County and New Jersey's largest city, with a Census Bureau estimate of 323,808 residents for July 2025 on 24.14 square miles of land. Most households rent, so a seller often deals with tenants already in the building. The city has five wards, and heavily industrial land around the airport and seaport sits mostly in the East and South wards, while homes cluster in the North, Central and West wards.

Newark housing and income facts, Census Bureau QuickFacts
MeasureNewark
Estimated residents, July 2025323,808
Owner-occupancy rate, 2020 to 202424.4%
Middle value of an owned home$373,700
Median gross rent$1,392
Households113,384
Median household income$52,060

The land slopes from about 230 feet in the western section down to sea level in the east, in a basin that drains toward the Passaic River. Historically the higher ground, around Forest Hill, High Street and Weequahic, drew the wealthier families. The East Ward's Ironbound is a dense district of apartment buildings and rowhouses, while the marshes on Newark Bay were reclaimed in the 1920s for the airport and Port Newark.

Which Newark neighborhoods and roads shape a sale?

Each ward has its own housing mix. The North Ward is centered on Branch Brook Park and takes in Broadway, Mount Pleasant, Upper Roseville and Forest Hill, where the Forest Hill Historic District holds older mansions and colonial homes. The West Ward covers Vailsburg, Ivy Hill, the West Side, Fairmount and Lower Roseville. The South Ward includes Weequahic, Clinton Hill and Dayton, and the Central Ward holds University Heights and Government Center.

Newark is served by the New Jersey Turnpike (Interstate 95), Interstate 280, Interstate 78, the Garden State Parkway, U.S. Routes 1/9 and 22, and Route 21. Newark Penn Station, east of downtown, carries PATH, NJ Transit and Amtrak trains, and the Newark Light Rail links it to Broad Street Station. In 2020, 40.3 percent of Newark households had no car, so a short walk to transit is a real selling point for many buyers.

More than 100,000 people commute to Newark each workday, and nearly 50,000 students attend its universities and medical and law schools. Newark Public Schools is the largest school system in the state.

How should I handle tax due when I sell a Newark house?

Ask Revenue Collections for a written statement covering every unpaid quarter, interest and any tax sale certificate, dated to the closing day. Whoever handles the closing pays that balance from the seller's proceeds, which clears the lien for the buyer.

  • List every quarter that is open, including prior-year balances, since those can already be in a tax sale.
  • Check whether a certificate was sold and recorded, and who holds it.
  • If an assessment appeal is pending, tell your closing attorney so the filing is accounted for at closing.
  • Plan for the seller-paid realty transfer fee on the deed.

More questions about Newark, NJ Property Tax Guide

Who do I call to find out what I owe on a Newark house?

Call Newark's Finance customer service on a weekday between 9 am and 4 pm at 973-733-3791, one of five tax lines the city lists. Ask for the amount through your closing date.

By what date must a Newark assessment petition arrive?

The deadline is April 1, or May 1 if a revaluation or reassessment was done. File Form A-1 with the Essex County Board of Taxation. Owners of property assessed above $1,000,000 can go straight to the Tax Court.

What interest does Newark charge on late taxes?

Interest can reach 8 percent on the first $1,500 and 18 percent on the balance above that, under state law. A penalty of up to 6 percent can follow when the delinquency is over $10,000 at year end.

Does paying part of my bill stop a tax sale?

A partial payment is credited to the oldest quarter first, which cuts that quarter's principal and interest but leaves later quarters open. Newark can still sell a certificate for prior years' taxes that remain unpaid.

Can I sell a Newark house that has a tax sale certificate on it?

Yes. The certificate amount and its interest come out of the sale price at closing, and the holder then discharges the lien. Get the payoff from the tax collector in writing so the title company can wire the exact amount.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who bills what in Lakewood

  • Tax Assessor handles assessment.

Lakewood by the numbers

Where is Lakewood, NJ, and how big has it become?

Lakewood is a township in Ocean County, New Jersey, and the county's most populous municipality. Wikipedia lists 24.68 square miles of land on the flat coastal plain, with the North Branch of the Metedeconk River along its northern edge and four man-made lakes inside the township. Brick Township, Jackson Township and Toms River border it in Ocean County, and Howell Township lies across the line in Monmouth County.

The township was incorporated in 1892 from part of Brick Township, and much of its housing stock arrived after the 1960s, when woods and cranberry bogs gave way to subdivisions. Population then climbed fast: 60,352 in 2000, 92,843 in 2010 and 135,158 in 2020. By the 2025 estimate, 143,765 people live in the township.

For a seller, that growth shows up in the tax records. Parcels range from older single-family lots near the lakes to newer builds and large condominium communities, so two houses a few blocks apart can carry very different assessments.

Who works on Lakewood property tax inside the Municipal Building?

Two desks inside the Municipal Building at 231 Third Street, Lakewood, NJ 08701, split the work. The Tax Assessor fixes the assessed value of each parcel, while the Tax Collector mails the bill and receives payment. The county tax board in Toms River hears assessment appeals.

  • Tax Assessor: 732-364-2500, extension 5248, open 8:30 AM to 5 PM according to the township assessor page. Ownership records, name and address changes and senior, disability and veteran deduction forms go through this office.
  • Tax Collector: 732-364-2500, open 9 AM to 5 PM according to the township collector page. Bring payment questions, payoff requests and tax sale concerns to this desk.
  • Ocean County Board of Taxation: receives appeals at the Courthouse on Washington Street in Toms River.

The collector's page adds that a new deed reaches the tax records when the Ocean County Clerk forwards it to the assessor, and the collector then works from the assessor's file. If a closing is close, ask the assessor to confirm the owner of record so the bill and any payoff request go to the right name.

What are the Lakewood due dates, and what does a late payment cost?

Lakewood taxes are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. The township gives a 10-day grace period, so a payment that reaches the office by the 10th carries no interest. The township counts days from the date it receives payment, and a postmark does not help.

Bills go out once a year in the summer with four coupons. The first two quarters equal half of the prior year's bill, and the last two reflect the rate struck for the current year, so they come out larger if the rate rose and smaller if it fell. The collector also states that an owner stays responsible for the tax even without a bill in hand, and that escrow with a lender does not change that.

Late-payment costs on the collector's page:

  • Interest of 8% a year on the first $1,500 of a delinquency.
  • Interest of 18% a year on every dollar over $1,500.
  • A 6% year-end penalty if the open balance of tax and interest on December 31 exceeds $10,000, with the whole amount then accruing at 18% from January 1.

A balance counts as current once all earlier bills are paid before the next quarter comes due.

What does a Lakewood property tax payoff look like at a sale?

A Lakewood house can be sold with tax owed, because the closing agent pays the open amount out of the seller's proceeds and records the payment. The seller needs a figure from the collector that runs through the closing date, including any accrued interest.

The bigger concern is a tax sale lien. Lakewood must hold a tax sale each year for the previous year's unpaid municipal charges, which covers water, sewer, maintenance liens and taxes. The 2026 online auction notice covered 2025 and earlier delinquencies and listed October 28, 2026 as the sale date. Selling at a tax sale does not transfer the house. A lien goes on the parcel instead, and the buyer of that lien earns interest until it is redeemed.

The collector explains that most lienholders record the lien with the Ocean County Clerk, and clear title cannot be issued while a recorded lien sits on the property. Liens must be redeemed in full with guaranteed funds. A lien held by the township allows foreclosure to begin six months after the sale, and a lien bought by a third party allows it after two years. A seller who sees a certificate on the parcel should ask the collector for the redemption amount before listing or signing a contract.

How can Lakewood owners challenge an assessment?

Owners challenge the assessed value, never the tax itself, and the deadline falls on April 1 of the year at issue. The assessor's page says a filing counts only when it arrives at the Ocean County Board of Taxation, so mail or drop it off with time to spare. The municipality cannot accept a petition meant for the county board.

The assessor mails a postcard notice on or before February 1 showing land, building and total value along with the prior year's tax. The same page lists the practical limits of an appeal:

  • Land and building values cannot be appealed separately.
  • Assessments of neighboring houses are not accepted as evidence of your value.
  • The first quarter's taxes and municipal charges must be paid before the appeal can be completed.
  • Skipping a certificate of occupancy does not avoid an assessment.

The assessor's office will review a value with an owner by appointment before any filing. The state's appeal guide adds that the burden of proof sits with the owner, who should attach three to five comparable sales, and that a county board decision can be taken to the Tax Court within 45 days.

How do Lakewood households and housing look in federal data?

The township's housing profile differs from most of New Jersey, mainly because households are large and young. Figures below come from Census QuickFacts for Lakewood township.

Persons under 1849.8%

Roughly half of Lakewood homes are rented, so many sellers here are landlords with tenants in place. A tenant's lease, rent roll and any open repair requests all matter to a buyer, and unpaid tax on a rental parcel creates the same lien risk as on an owner-occupied one.

Which tax relief programs apply to Lakewood homeowners?

State programs help eligible owners, and the township assessor's office handles the local deductions. The assessor's page names the senior citizen deduction, the disability deduction, the surviving spouse deduction, the veteran deductions and the disabled veteran exemption, with forms in the township's download center.

The New Jersey Division of Taxation's relief page says the fiscal year 2027 budget funds the Senior Freeze, ANCHOR and Stay NJ programs. The deadline for the 2025 application was November 2, 2026. The state also warns against clicking links in unsolicited texts or emails about relief benefits.

A sale can change eligibility, so a seller who receives a benefit should ask the state program office how a mid-year move affects the claim.

More questions about Lakewood, NJ Property Tax Guide

What is the Lakewood property tax appeal deadline?

April 1 of the year being appealed, and the petition must be received by the Ocean County Board of Taxation in Toms River. Lakewood's assessor page states that a filing is complete only on receipt, and a petition handed to the township does not count.

Can I sell my Lakewood house if I owe back taxes?

Yes. Your closing agent requests a payoff from the Lakewood tax collector and pays the balance from your sale proceeds. If a tax sale certificate already exists on the parcel, the lien must be redeemed in full with guaranteed funds before clear title can pass.

How much interest does Lakewood charge on late taxes?

Interest runs at 8% a year on the first $1,500 of delinquency and 18% on the amount above that. A 6% year-end penalty applies when open tax and interest on December 31 exceed $10,000, and the township counts from the day it receives the payment.

Which Lakewood office explains my assessed value?

Call the Tax Assessor at 732-364-2500, extension 5248, in the Municipal Building at 231 Third Street. The office reviews values by appointment, and the township's page lists weekday hours of 8:30 AM to 5 PM.

Why is my Lakewood second-half tax bill different from the first half?

The first two quarters are set at half of last year's bill, while the last two reflect the rate struck for the current year. If the budgets of the county, school district and township rose, the second half grows, and if they fell it shrinks.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Local notes

Where is Middletown, NJ, and what shapes its housing?

Middletown is a township in northern Monmouth County and the county's largest municipality by population. Wikipedia gives it 58.72 square miles in total, of which 40.95 are land and 17.78 are water, mostly Sandy Hook Bay, Raritan Bay and the Navesink River. That water frontage explains why a good share of its houses sit near the shoreline or on creek lots.

The township was formed on October 31, 1693 and incorporated under the Township Act of 1798. Railroad service arrived in 1875, and the area slowly turned from fishing and farming villages into a commuter suburb. The township website lists five historic districts: Chapel Hill, Locust, Monmouth Hills, Navesink and Middletown Village.

The township spans eleven ZIP codes, and their postal names include Middletown, Belford, Lincroft, Locust, Navesink, Port Monmouth and Leonardo. A mailing address with one of those names can still sit inside the Township of Middletown for tax purposes, so check the block and lot rather than the postal town.

Which Middletown office does what with property tax?

Middletown splits the job between an assessment office and a collection division, and both sit in the Finance Department at 1 Kings Highway, Middletown, NJ 07748. Assessment questions go to the Tax Assessor, and the collector bills and collects only.

  • Tax Collection: 732-615-2086. Payment hours run 8:00 AM to 3:45 PM and office hours are 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, Monday to Friday, per the township collection page.
  • Tax Assessor: handles value, ownership and address changes, and senior and veteran relief paperwork. The township's assessment page links to the Monmouth County record search for assessed values, sales and property record cards.
  • Sewerage Authority: 732-495-1010 for delinquent sewer charges, which are billed separately from the tax bill.

The township says the bill combines municipal, library, school, open space and county taxes. Because those levies come from different bodies, the Middletown collector cannot explain a school or county budget line and will direct you to the taxing authority.

What are the Middletown property tax due dates and the grace period?

Middletown taxes are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. A 10-day grace period normally applies, and a tenth day that lands on a weekend or holiday pushes the deadline to the following business day. The last moment to pay without interest is 3:45 PM on the final day of the grace period.

The township states that the State of New Jersey does not accept postmarks, so a payment must be in the office on time. Interest on late payments is governed by N.J.S.A. 54:4-66. Failing to receive a bill does not cancel the tax under N.J.S.A. 54:4-64, so the owner is responsible for asking the collector what is due.

Bills go out once a year. The first-half amount is a preliminary half of the previous year's taxes, and the second-half bill subtracts that estimate from the final total once the rate is set. The collection page asks sellers to hand the bill to the new owner or the buyer's paying agent at closing. A duplicate bill carries a charge.

How does the Middletown tax sale work, and how does it affect a seller?

Every New Jersey municipality must hold at least one tax sale a year, and Middletown runs an accelerated electronic sale. For 2026 the township listed December 17, 2026 as the sale date. Payments received after 3:45 PM on November 10, 2026 had to be guaranteed funds such as an attorney trust check, title company check, cashier's check or money order, and card or ACH payments were unavailable after that time.

An unpaid parcel picks up added costs once it enters the sale process:

  • A 2% cost of sale, with a $15 minimum and a $100 maximum.
  • A $25 mailing fee for each of two scheduled mailings.
  • Delinquent taxes plus interest, added to those fees for the total due.

The township says these fees cannot be waived, and a notice that goes astray does not void the sale. It also warns that a tax lien gives the buyer no right to possess the property, which comes only through foreclosure. A seller who is behind should ask the collector for an exact payoff and give it to the title company early. Cash payments must be exact, because excess cash goes to the next quarter and no change is returned.

How did Middletown's 2026 assessments change, and how are appeals filed?

The township reports that the aggregate preliminary net value of Middletown for tax year 2026 was 7.94% above 2025. Higher total value does not mean every bill rises by that percentage, because the rate falls as total value climbs. An owner whose assessment grew less than 7.94% takes on a smaller share of the municipal levy, and one whose assessment grew more takes on a larger share.

The same page gives the appeal window for 2026 assessments: January 15, or April 1 if the assessment exceeds $1 million. Monmouth County uses an alternate calendar, so the statewide April 1 date does not govern ordinary houses here. Petitions can be filed through secure.njappealonline.com. Changes agreed with the assessor after May 15, 2026 take effect in tax year 2027.

Before filing, compare your value with closed sales on the township's interactive sales map, which leaves out distressed sales. The state's appeal guide says property taxes cannot be appealed, only the assessment, and that evidence should be dated before the October 1 assessment date.

What do Census numbers show for Middletown homeowners?

Middletown is a heavily owner-occupied suburb with high incomes and long commutes, according to Census QuickFacts.

Middletown township figures from the Census Bureau, 2020-2024 survey period
MeasureMiddletown township
Population, April 2020 Census67,106
Owner-occupied housing rate85.7%
Typical value of an owner's home$608,300
Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage$3,107
Households25,211
Median household income$141,810
Average commute34.9 minutes

With about 86% of occupied homes lived in by their owners, most Middletown sales involve a family selling a primary residence, and many include a mortgage payoff alongside any tax balance.

Does Middletown's historic designation affect a sale?

It can. The township's Landmarks Commission reviews work on structures inside the five historic districts, and owners planning additions or changes need a Certificate of Appropriateness. A buyer of a house in Middletown Village, Navesink, Locust, Chapel Hill or Monmouth Hills should know that exterior plans may go through that review.

Houses outside those districts follow ordinary township permit rules. If you are unsure which applies, ask the township with the block and lot number from your tax bill.

More questions about Middletown, NJ Property Tax Guide

When is the last day to pay Middletown property tax without interest?

It is the last day of a 10-day grace period after each due date of February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, by 3:45 PM. A weekend or holiday on the tenth pushes the deadline to the following business day.

Can I sell a Middletown house with unpaid taxes?

Yes. Ask the Middletown tax collector for a payoff figure, and your closing agent settles it out of the sale money. If the parcel has entered the tax sale process, added costs apply and guaranteed funds are required.

What is the appeal deadline for a Middletown assessment?

For 2026 assessments the township lists January 15, or April 1 when the assessment is over $1 million. Monmouth County follows an alternate calendar, and filing can be done through secure.njappealonline.com.

Who do I contact if my Middletown sewer bill is overdue?

Call the Township of Middletown Sewerage Authority at 732-495-1010. Delinquent sewer charges are separate from the property tax bill, and the township said it would sell delinquent sewer charges in 2026.

Does a postmark count for a Middletown tax payment?

No. The township says New Jersey does not accept postmarks, so the payment must be received in the office by 3:45 PM on or before the last day of the grace period.
